summary: No additional Kong-specific filing, financing, secondary transaction, acquisition, executive change, commercial disclosure, or material product release was found after the earlier September 3 review. A strong AI-driven Snowflake result supported software-sector sentiment, but it does not establish Kong revenue quality or justify changing the 72-point thesis, model defaults, or valuation references.

items.title: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 reaches general availability
items.summary: The production-supported release reduces product-execution risk around Kong's AI-control-plane strategy. It strengthens the product-position score, while valuation inputs remain unchanged until commercial traction or financial contribution is disclosed.
confirmed: Kong says AI Gateway 2.0 is generally available and production-supported in Konnect with its own runtime and control plane.

The release adds MCP Server Bundling with per-caller tool visibility, modality-aware cost governance, Kong Identity principals, expanded model-provider support, and native AWS IAM authentication for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose customer adoption, bookings, incremental ARR, pricing, margins, or financial contribution.
The pace of customer migration from existing Gateway AI plugins to the standalone product is unknown.

items.title: Kong adds native NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing
items.summary: The integration lets Kong preserve credentials, policy, metering, and audit controls while an external decision service selects models. It strengthens ecosystem relevance and AI cost optimization, but commercial contribution was not disclosed.
confirmed: Kong described a native pattern in which NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard selects a model and Kong AI Gateway retains connectivity, governance, and traffic management.
NVIDIA separately listed Kong as delivering NeMo Switchyard routing natively through Kong AI Gateway.
uncertain: Kong and NVIDIA did not disclose joint customers, contractual economics, usage, or incremental revenue.

items.title: Harness partnership expands from API Gateway to AI Gateway
items.summary: The generally available integration adds AI asset discovery and behavioral protection around Kong-routed LLM, MCP, and agent traffic. It supports ecosystem breadth but does not establish material revenue.
confirmed: Harness and Kong expanded their existing API security integration to Kong AI Gateway.
Harness says AI Discovery and AI Protection are generally available to joint customers.
uncertain: Joint-customer count, attach rate, pricing, bookings, and revenue contribution were not disclosed.

items.title: Kong reports 72% year-over-year EMEA customer growth
items.summary: This is the strongest new commercial signal in the review window. Rapid regional customer growth and named enterprise and AI-native wins improve confidence in demand, although the regional figure cannot be treated as company-wide ARR growth.
confirmed: Kong reported a 72% year-over-year increase in EMEA customers and 71% headcount growth in the region over two years.
Kong named ING Bank, First Abu Dhabi Bank, Mistral, and PolyAI as notable new customers and opened offices in Paris and Milan.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose the starting customer count, regional revenue, company-wide growth, ARR, churn, retention, or sales efficiency.
The 71% headcount expansion may support growth but also increases operating expense.

items.title: Kong Agent Gateway reaches production-ready GA
items.summary: Agent Gateway extended Kong from LLM and MCP traffic into governed agent-to-agent communication. Together with Context Mesh and later AI Gateway 2.0, it supports a broader platform-position score.
confirmed: Kong made Agent Gateway generally available and production-ready in AI Gateway 3.14.
Kong says the product governs LLM, MCP, and A2A traffic and is available to all Kong Konnect customers as part of AI Gateway.
uncertain: The A2A market remains early, and Kong did not disclose Agent Gateway adoption, pricing, bookings, or revenue.

items.title: StepStone fund marks Kong preferred shares near $10.24
items.summary: An audited fund filing provides an external private-market reference close to the user's later roughly $10 secondary marker. Because it is a Level 3 preferred-share valuation rather than a liquid common-share trade, it does not change the model.
confirmed: StepStone Private Venture and Growth Fund reported 1,211,663 Kong preferred shares at a $12,412,033 fair value as of March 31, 2026, implying approximately $10.24 per preferred share.
The same position had a reported cost of $12,123,382, or approximately $10.01 per preferred share.
uncertain: The share series, liquidation preference, conversion terms, fully diluted capitalization, and valuation methodology for the specific Kong position were not disclosed in the schedule.
The fund mark is not evidence of a current liquid secondary price or an IPO price.

items.title: Kong appoints IPO-experienced CFO Bruce Felt
items.summary: Hiring a CFO who has led three software companies through public offerings improves Kong's organizational readiness. It is a preparation signal, not confirmation of an IPO filing or timetable.
confirmed: Kong appointed Bruce Felt as CFO to help scale the business through its next growth stage.
Kong says Felt took FullTime Software, SuccessFactors, and Domo public as CFO and has experience with acquisitions and global expansion.
uncertain: Kong did not say that Felt was hired specifically to execute an IPO and did not announce a filing, exchange, underwriters, or timetable.

items.title: Kong and Solace connect APIs, events, and AI traffic
items.summary: The technology partnership expands Kong's governed data-path story into real-time event streams. It is strategically relevant, while its adoption and economics remain unknown.
confirmed: Solace joined Kong's Premium Technology Partner Program.
The companies described a combined control plane for APIs, events, LLMs, and MCP servers with shared governance and observability.
uncertain: The announcement did not disclose customer deployments, commercial terms, bookings, or revenue contribution.

items.title: Context Mesh turns enterprise APIs into governed agent tools
items.summary: Context Mesh and MCP Registry broaden Kong's addressable workflow from managing traffic to discovering, generating, deploying, and governing tools for AI agents. The product case improves, but monetization is not yet quantified.
confirmed: Kong launched Context Mesh to discover enterprise APIs, transform them into agent-consumable tools, and deploy them with runtime governance.
Kong positioned Context Mesh alongside MCP Registry, AI Gateway, and Event Gateway across the AI data path.
uncertain: Customer adoption, pricing, incremental ARR, and competitive differentiation at scale were not disclosed.

items.title: OpenMeter technology reaches Kong Konnect
items.summary: Kong moved the OpenMeter acquisition into a Konnect product for AI cost control, chargeback, and monetization. This reduces integration risk, but uptake and financial impact remain undisclosed.
confirmed: Kong launched Konnect Metering & Billing following the OpenMeter acquisition.
The product targets AI cost controls, showback, chargeback, and usage-based monetization.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose product adoption, attach rates, pricing, bookings, revenue, or margin contribution.

items.title: Kong centers its 2026 strategy on AI connectivity
items.summary: The strategy reinforces Kong's position as a control layer for APIs and AI traffic, but it does not supply the audited growth, margin, retention, or share-count evidence needed for a valuation upgrade.
confirmed: Kong described AI connectivity, large-enterprise adoption, organizational expansion, and regional investment as strategic priorities.
uncertain: Revenue contribution, adoption rates, growth, and margin effects were not disclosed.

items.title: OpenMeter adds usage metering and billing to Kong's platform
items.summary: The acquisition broadens Kong's monetization layer for API and AI workloads. It improves strategic breadth, while integration quality and financial contribution remain unproven.
confirmed: Kong acquired OpenMeter and described native usage metering and billing as part of the expanded platform.
uncertain: Purchase terms, integration economics, customer uptake, and incremental ARR were not disclosed.
